HFCL FY26 Annual Report Key Takeaways 🧵

• Strong FY26: Revenue grew 21.8% to ₹4,949 Cr, EBITDA +63.2% to ₹827 Cr and PAT +90.1% to ₹329 Cr.

• Margins expanding: EBITDA margin improved sharply to 16.7% from 12.5%, driven by better product mix and higher capacity utilisation.

• Business mix changing: Product-led revenue rose to 62% from 42%, while private customers increased to 84% from 65%.

• Exports taking off: Export contribution jumped to 41.4% from 12.2% in FY25, with >70% of cable production now serving international markets.

• Big global win: ₹10,159 Cr ($1.1B) OFC (Optical Fiber Cable) supply agreement with a global hyperscaler. Management targets exports at >50% of revenue by FY27.

• Strong visibility: Order book stood at ₹21,206 Cr in March 2026 and increased to ₹26,665 Cr by June 2026.

• Profitability is shifting: Telecom Products generated ₹2,931 Cr revenue and ₹764 Cr segment profit, while Turnkey Contracts generated ₹1,875 Cr revenue but a ₹113 Cr loss.

• Strategic pivot working: HFCL is moving from lower-margin project execution towards higher-margin, product-led businesses.

• Capacity expansion: OF capacity targeted at 38.5 mn fkm (fiber kilometer) and OFC capacity at 56.36 mn fkm by July 2028, with ~₹580 Cr being invested in backward integration into preforms.

• Defence opportunity: Defence revenue targeted at ₹500 Cr in FY27 vs ₹77 Cr in FY26, with a ~₹2,189 Cr defence/aerospace pipeline.

• Aerospace entry: Proposed acquisition brings an export-oriented ₹1,890 Cr order book, while a 1,000-acre defence facility is being developed in Andhra Pradesh.

• BharatNet optionality: HFCL has secured >₹7,335 Cr of Phase III contracts and sees upcoming opportunities worth >₹50,000 Cr.

• R&D focus: 229 R&D professionals are working across 5G, Wi-Fi, AI-enabled networking and emerging 6G technologies.

• Balance sheet: Debt increased to ₹1,713 Cr, but Net Debt/Equity remained comfortable at 0.34x.

• Key concern - cash flow: Operating cash flow was -₹335 Cr despite ₹329 Cr PAT, mainly due to higher inventory and receivables supporting the growing order book.

Overall, FY26 marks a meaningful transformation - from projects to products, domestic to global, and telecom towards a broader connectivity + defence + aerospace platform.

The Indian IT sector is having an identity crisis.

Nifty IT is down ~17% YTD. TCS and Wipro are down 26–30%.
Coforge? Up. Persistent? Quietly holding ground.

Same sector. Completely different story.

Here's what's actually happening:

US clients are deploying AI agents.
One agent replaces 10 deployed analysts.
Headcount-per-deal drops.
Revenue-per-employee drops.
TCV goes up (deals look big on paper).
But actual revenue doesn't follow.
EPS growth slows. P/E de-rates.

That's the chain. And large caps are stuck in it.

Mid-caps like Coforge cracked the code differently:
Smaller teams. Faster deployment. Outcome-based pricing.
AI augments delivery instead of deflating it.

The 4 metrics that'll separate winners in Q2 FY27:
→ % of revenue explicitly tagged as AI revenue
→ Agent-per-FTE ratio (are they replacing or augmenting?)
→ GenAI margin impact disclosed (accretive or dilutive?)
→ Deal structure shift — FTE-based vs outcome-based %

TCV is a lagging indicator now.
Revenue realization is the only number that matters.

The irony? Bigger the firm, bigger the deflation surface.

Q2 results start October. September is your preview window.

#QuestioningConvictionMuscle | Week ended 4 Sep 2026

The S&P 500 edged higher while Nifty fell for a fourth week.

Fear rose, yet volatility stayed subdued. Is this stress, rotation, or denial?

Market Pulse
S&P 500: +0.1%, closing 7,718.60.
Nifty 50: -1.2%, closing 23,897.70.

CNN Fear & Greed fell from 52, Neutral, to 42, Fear.
India's MMI fell from 49.46 to 43.87, both Fear.

US VIX ended at 14.53, up 0.10 point.
India VIX ended at 10.68, unchanged for the week despite a 5.8% Friday fall.

US and India Sector Divergence

US energy led as crude rose roughly 10%. Technology ranked next, but hardware strength hid a software selloff. Utilities also advanced. Equal-weight S&P 500 fell 0.8% while the NYSE 100 gained 0.7%, exposing narrow leadership beneath the flat headline index.

India was broader risk-off: 12 of 16 major sectors fell. Autos lost 4%, midcaps fell 1.5%, while smallcaps gained 0.1%. Coal India rose 3.6% on better earnings visibility. Capital-market stocks bounced Friday after SEBI said it would review derivatives settlement pricing. Price says selective rotation, sentiment says fear.

Announcements That Matter
• TCS, weekend: HyperVault secured 264 acres for a phased Hyderabad AI data-centre campus up to 1GW. TCS and partners expect investment up to ₹70,000 crore. The project is not operating. Watch customers, power and commissioning.

• Broadcom: Q3 revenue rose 86% to $29.6 billion. AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7 billion, up 221%, while free cash flow was $13.7 billion. Q4 guidance is $34.8 billion. Watch whether growth holds without weaker margins.

• Nvidia: Agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion. Nvidia says the platform will remain open, multi-cloud and multi-accelerator. The strategic prize is developer distribution. Watch regulatory review and whether non-Nvidia hardware retains equal access.

• Sun Pharma: Joined nine manufacturers in US most-favoured-nation pricing agreements covering state Medicaid and future innovative medicines. The group committed at least $19.6 billion to US manufacturing. Watch company-specific pricing, capex and margin disclosure before assigning winners or losers.

• ICICI Bank and LIC, weekend: RBI approved LIC to lift its aggregate ICICI Bank holding to 9.99% of paid-up capital or voting rights within one year. Permission, not purchase. Watch shareholding disclosures.

• Adobe: Anil Chakravarthy will become CEO on 1 Dec; Shantanu Narayen moves to executive chair. With earnings due 10 Sep, the test is whether leadership change sharpens Adobe's AI monetisation story.

• Lululemon: Q2 revenue fell 4% and comparable sales fell 9%. Management guided Q3 revenue down 10% to 11% and FY2026 revenue down 5% to 7%. Watch Americas demand, markdowns and tariff-adjusted margins.

Small Company, Big Signal

E2E Networks signed a binding term sheet worth about ₹1,000 crore for Nvidia Blackwell cloud GPUs and services through June 2029, roughly four times FY2026 revenue. 

A term sheet is not recognised revenue. Billing milestones, customer concentration, utilisation and depreciation will decide the economics.

Cross-Border Government Signals

Global Signal, India Implication: BLS reported 162,000 US payroll additions in August. Resilient labour demand keeps US rate risk alive, raising the hurdle for Indian valuations and foreign flows.

India Signal, Global Implication: MoSPI reported Q1 goods-and-services exports up 25.8%, imports up 30.5% and machinery imports up 51.5%.

India is exporting faster while importing capital goods even faster, supporting global suppliers but increasing exposure to oil, currencies and financing costs.

Policy Winners & Losers

Potential winners include domestic data-centre suppliers and US manufacturing beneficiaries. 

Potential losers include pharma products exposed to lower public-program pricing. 

SEBI's settlement-price review may help market platforms, but final rules will determine the economics.

Consumer Temperature, Measured

RBI's July surveys covered 5,987 urban and 8,581 rural respondents. Current Situation indices fell to 88.3 from 90.7 in cities and 91.7 from 95.2 in rural areas. Yet non-essential-spending net responses improved to 3.3 from -0.8 urban and 32.4 from 30.1 rural. Households felt worse about conditions while reporting more discretionary spending.

Where Capital Is Crowding

US concentration is visible: equal-weight S&P 500 fell 0.8% while the NYSE 100 gained 0.7%, and hardware beat software. 

India's clearest crowding evidence remains primary markets: average IPO subscriptions rose to 59.1 times from 24.5 times, while listing gains climbed to 19.5% from 5.7%. 

AI announcements show capital clustering, but announcements alone do not prove a crowded trade. Watch breadth, pricing discipline and capex returns.

Greed & Pain

Greed sits in primary-market demand and the expanding AI-capex narrative, where announcements can be priced before utilisation and returns appear.

Pain sits in Indian autos, US consumer discretionary, software weakness and higher yields. The disagreement: fear gauges worsened, yet both volatility indices stayed low.

Failed Expectations

India's 7.8% real GDP growth did not lift Nifty. Strong US payrolls of 162,000 were good economic news, yet yields rose and the S&P 500 fell Friday. Good data did not mean easy money.

Week Ahead, 7 to 13 Sep

• 7 Sep: US markets closed for Labor Day.
• 10 Sep: US August PPI at 8:30 am ET. ECB decision at 14:15 CET, press conference at 14:45 and projections at 15:45. Oracle and Adobe report after the US close.
• 11 Sep: US August CPI at 8:30 am ET.

Inflation and the ECB will test the rate narrative. Oracle and Adobe will test whether AI spending is producing revenue beyond semiconductors.

Strongest Counterargument

The bearish read may be too neat. S&P 500, Nasdaq, Russell 2000 and Indian smallcaps gained while volatility stayed low. This may be rotation under pressure. Broader participation, easing yields and stable guidance would support that view. Rising volatility alongside weaker breadth and earnings cuts would refute it.

Conviction Check

• Is oil now the binding constraint for India's earnings and inflation?
• Can AI infrastructure earn returns before hardware depreciates?
• Does US software weakness challenge the AI monetisation story?
• Are IPO buyers pricing growth, scarcity, or exit liquidity?

One Rabbit Hole
Track who captures each ₹100 of AI spending: chips, networking, power, cooling, cloud operators, or software. That may matter more than capex headlines.

Which assumption in this week's market story would you challenge first?

We screened Q1 FY27 (April to June 2026) results for midcap CDMO names with 50%+ company-wide revenue growth.

Short answer: the list is thin. Most CRDMO players run mixed books (API plus formulations plus contract manufacturing), project timing is lumpy, and several of the cleanest names have already moved into largecap territory.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗰𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗻 𝗵𝗶𝘁

𝗡𝗲𝘂𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗟𝗮𝗯𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘀 (market cap around ₹25,000 crore)
Revenue up around 116 to 119% YoY to around ₹641 to 650 crore. Commercial CMS/CDMO projects did the heavy lifting, with export traction across Europe and the US. Margins expanded sharply alongside.

𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗴, 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝟱𝟬%

𝗦𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗽𝗮 𝗠𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗲 (around ₹18,800 crore): revenue up 43 to 45%. Formulations more than doubled, specialty CDMO picking up.

𝗔𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗶 𝗣𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗯𝘀 (around ₹7,800 crore): revenue up 39 to 42%, with fresh capex announced for additional capacity.

𝗜𝗻𝗻𝗼𝘃𝗮 𝗖𝗮𝗽𝘁𝗮𝗯 (around ₹6,700 crore): revenue up 34%. CDMO segment, at around 70% of the book, grew around 32%.

𝗔𝗸𝘂𝗺𝘀 𝗗𝗿𝘂𝗴𝘀 (around ₹12,000 crore): topline up 14%, core CDMO revenue up 18 to 19%.

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗱 𝗕𝗶𝗼𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵 (around ₹16,400 crore): up 26%. API led, with CDMO ambitions.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗶𝘇𝗲 𝗳𝗶𝗹𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝘀 𝗱𝗼𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲

Laurus Labs reported CDMO revenue up around 67%, and Divi's CDMO grew around 50%. Both sit outside the midcap bucket, so they fall out of this screen even though the underlying trend is identical.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱

The structural story is intact: China plus one, more commercial stage work shifting to India, peptides, ADCs, complex chemistry.

But one quarter tells you very little in this business. Shipment timing and the development versus commercial mix can swing a quarter hard in either direction. What matters is order book conversion, client concentration and utilisation tracked across four to six quarters, not a single YoY print.

Which midcap CDMO names are on your list that we have missed?

Gold financing stocks have had a strong year. IIFL up 50%, Manappuram 19%, FedFina 18%, Muthoot 3%, CSB down 8%.

Three things went right at once. Gold ran to records through FY26, which meant a lender could advance more against the same jewellery without changing anything about how it operated. Unsecured credit tightened after the microfinance mess, pushing borrowers toward the one asset most Indian households already own. And the RBI's new framework, which the market had braced for, landed friendlier than feared: more headroom on small consumption loans, no cap at all on income-generation loans, and no prior approval needed to open branches. That last one is why every lender in the group is suddenly expanding.

The first of those has now reversed. Domestic gold fell roughly 15% between the end of January and the end of June. That matters more in this sector than in most, because a gold loan book is short. It rolls inside a year, so it reflects current prices rather than prices from a long time ago. While the metal was rising, growth arrived without anyone having to do much. Now it has to come from grams pledged, and tonnage grows in single digits a quarter, not in the forties.

This is why FY27 guidance sits so far below what FY26 delivered. Muthoot grew 49% last year and is guiding 15% for this one.

The structural case is intact. Most gold lending in India still happens outside the formal system, with pawnbrokers and jewellers, and that share moves to organised lenders every year. Branch expansion is easier than it has been in over a decade. Demand from rural and semi-urban borrowers is steady and not especially rate-sensitive.

So the sector probably keeps growing. It just stops growing the easy way. FY26 was a year when the collateral did the work. FY27 is a year when the lender has to.

Coal India Output and Dispatch Set to Accelerate as Monsoon Effect Wanes

✅As the intense rains over coal command regions show clear signs of easing, coal production and supplies at Coal India Limited (CIL) are gathering pace and are set to improve further from here on. Despite prolonged spells of rain through July and August, particularly across the East-Central parts, CIL maintained a steady supply run. 

✅During April–August of the current fiscal, CIL supplied 322.90 million Tonnes (MT) of coal, 6.70% higher than the 302.60 MT supplied during the corresponding period last year.

✅The easing rainfall is already bringing relief on the ground. Coal beds that had turned sticky and wet after prolonged rain exposure are now drying out, making freshly mined coal free-flowing and considerably easier to transfer, handle and dispatch through Coal Handling Plants (CHPs). 

✅Coal seams at lower mine horizons that had been submerged are being restored to production through augmented pumping, while repair of internal haul roads is progressing in full swing.

✅Mines across CIL are consequently stepping up preparations to return to full operational pace, with the focus firmly on ensuring that production and coal movement pick up quickly as ground conditions continue to improve. 

✅While average daily coal production during the rain-affected first three days of September stood at around 1.36 MT per day, it rose to approximately 1.7 MT per day  on 04.09.2026, even with just a single day's respite from rain.

4 weeks of losses. Auto sector down 4.5%. But small caps hit a record high.

Here is everything that moved the Indian market this week (August 31 – September 4, 2026). Save it, share it, bookmark it.

- Sensex: 76,515 (down 1%)
- Nifty: 23,897 (down 1.1%)

- SmallCap: Up 0.2% (fresh record high)
- India VIX: Dropped 0.5% (less fear in the market)
- Nifty has now fallen for four straight weeks. This is the longest losing streak in five months.

DAY BY DAY BREAKDOWN

- Monday: Flat to negative, closed at 24,080
- Tuesday: Boring day, closed at 24,055
- Wednesday: Dropped to 23,914
- Thursday: Slipped further to 23,873
- Friday: Small bounce to 23,897
Net result? A weak week that never really recovered. Four down days out of five.

WHO MADE MONEY THIS WEEK

- Tata Power +4.5% (order wins and upgrades)
- Solar Industries +4.2% (defence momentum)
- Coal India +3.8% (strong volumes)
- Reliance +3.1% (oil and gas rebound)
- TCS +2.5% (IT safe haven)
- Tejas Networks +8.2%
- The New India Assurance +17.7%
- Wockhardt +7%
- Pine Labs +6.3%
- ESDS Software listed at 108% premium on Friday
- Priority Jewels listed at 18% premium

WHO GOT HURT

- Adani Energy Solutions -12.8%
- Adani Enterprises -7.3%
- TVS Motor -6.3%
- Eicher Motors -5.8%
- KEI Industries -12.4%
- RR Kabel -13.3%
- Zee Entertainment -11.9%
- Kaynes Technology -10.5%
- Maruti Suzuki fell 5.1%. M&M lost 4.9%. When auto sector sneezes, the whole market catches a cold.

SECTOR PERFORMANCE

Green zones: IT, Oil and Gas, Private Banks

Red zones: Auto (down 4.5%), FMCG (down 2.9%), Media (down 2.8%), Consumer Durables (down 2.6%), Healthcare (down 2%)

Mixed: Metals bounced on Friday but still ended the week down

Auto was the worst performer by a mile. Royal Enfield 350cc plus volumes dropped 13% year on year. That spooked everyone.

THE BIG DRAMA: CRUDE OIL NEAR $96

Brent crude surged near $96 during the week because of West Asia tensions. India imports most of its oil. Higher crude means higher inflation and a bigger import bill. The market hates that.

Things calmed down by Friday after some diplomatic moves but the risk is still there. Any escalation next week and crude will spike again.

WHAT OUTSIDE INDIA DID TO US

- US Fed: Governor Christopher Waller signaled support for keeping rates unchanged. That gave markets some relief on Friday.
- US Jobs Data: Came in softer than expected. This boosted risk appetite and helped the Friday bounce.
- US 30-year bond yield stayed elevated at 5.25%. Global investors remain scared of US rates.
- FII Selling: Foreign investors sold Rs 5,612 crore this week. They have sold for three consecutive weeks now. Total FII outflows in 2026 have crossed Rs 2.3 lakh crore.
- DII Buying: Domestic institutions bought Rs 23,156 crore this week. They basically saved us from a much bigger crash.

The Tug-of-War: When US bond yields rise, FIIs sell. When DIIs buy, they balance it out. This fight continues every single day.

Rupee Strengthened: The rupee gained 89 paise to Rs 94.49 per dollar. This is a two month high. The RBI's FCNR scheme mobilized over 127 billion dollars in NRI inflows.

IPO MARKET WAS ON FIRE

- ESDS Software listed at 108% premium on Friday.
- Priority Jewels listed at 18% premium.

The pipeline is massive. Six IPOs are set to launch on a single day next week. That is a record.

- Rentomojo is coming with a Rs 1,255 crore issue.
- Karamtanga Engineering is coming with Rs 875 crore.
- Manipal Payment Solutions is coming with Rs 805 crore.
- LCC Projects is coming with Rs 427 crore.
- Glass Wall Systems is coming with Rs 428 crore.

SEBI cleared four more IPOs including NSE. Hero Motors is also in the pipeline. Jio Platforms IPO is still on the horizon.

Average IPO subscriptions doubled to 59 times in July-August compared to 24 times in April-June. Retail investors are eating well.

COMPANY NEWS THAT MOVED STOCKS

- HDFC Bank CEO decided to step down. The stock initially gained 2.5% but then reversed and touched a fresh 52-week low. This one needs watching.
- ITC Infotech announced plans to acquire 22% stake in Happiest Minds and merge the two tech businesses. ITC gained 4% on the news.
- Sterlite Technologies board approved a Rs 3,000 crore capex programme. They are targeting 50 percent capacity increase by 2029. Stock rose 5%.
- Power Grid bagged a transmission project in Gujarat worth Rs 1,152 crore per annum.
- L&T continues to bag massive orders from the Middle East.
- Adani Energy got a Rs 4,700 crore order earlier but still got hammered this week.
- Bharat Forge signed MOUs with FN Herstal for small arms manufacturing and with Thales for rocket systems. Defence orders keep flowing.
- Indian Energy Exchange recorded its highest ever monthly electricity traded volume at 13,938 million units. That is up 20 percent year on year.

HIDDEN GEMS NOBODY IS TALKING ABOUT

- Welspun Corp had strong gains in the small cap space.
- Angel One gained 4 percent after 20 percent gross client acquisition growth.
- Ramco Systems gained 4 percent after signing an MOU with Safran Helicopter Engines.
- Shanthi Gears gained 6 percent after appointing a new CFO.
- Lenskart Solutions, LIC Housing Finance, and IDFC First Bank were key mid-cap gainers.

The real money is often where nobody is looking.

ECONOMIC SIGNALS

India GDP grew at 7.8 percent in the first quarter of this financial year. That beat market expectations. Exports and investment drove the growth.

India Inc sales grew roughly 20 percent year on year. Manufacturing is back.

GST collections remain robust. The economic narrative is strong.

August auto sales numbers were healthy. But the market still punished auto stocks because of concerns about future growth.

Steel sector demand is firm and margins are getting better.

Power sector is getting tailwinds from both policy and global shifts.

The rupee stayed soft through most of the week but strengthened on Friday.

TECHNICAL LEVELS FOR MONDAY

- Nifty support at 23,670 to 23,470. Break below this and expect more selling.
- Nifty resistance at 24,120 to 24,320. Cross above this and bulls take charge.
- Nifty is currently at 23,897.
- Bank Nifty support at 57,000 to 57,200. Current level is 57,369.
- Midcap support at 23,020 to 22,820. Current level is 23,168.
- Smallcap resistance at 18,600 to 18,800. Current level is 18,481.
- India VIX dropped but still above 10. Less fear but also less conviction.

YOUR MONDAY CHECKLIST

- Check before 9:15 AM:
- How did US markets close on Friday? They rallied after softer jobs data.
- Asian markets on Monday morning. They set the mood for the day.
- Crude oil direction. It eased by Friday but West Asia is still a risk.
- US inflation data is coming next week. That will decide the Fed's next move.
- West Asia tensions. Any escalation equals crude spike equals market crash.

Stocks to watch:

- IT stocks like TCS and Infosys have momentum as defensive plays.
- Auto stocks like Maruti, M&M, and TVS are weak. Avoid for now.
- Power stocks like Tata Power and Power Grid have policy tailwinds.
- Defence stocks like HAL and BDL have government orders flowing.
- HDFC Bank has CEO stepping down. Expect volatility.

EVENTS THIS WEEK

- Skyways Air IPO listing was due on September 1. Grey market premium was at 32 percent.
- Apana Logistics SME IPO opens on September 7.
- Glass Wall Systems IPO opens on September 8.
- Six IPOs open on September 9 including Rentomojo, Karamtanga, Manipal Payment, LCC Projects and Vinod Texworld.
- Vinod Texworld SME IPO opens on September 9.
- Apana Logistics listing is tentatively on September 15.
- Glass Wall Systems listing is tentatively on September 16.

SEPTEMBER WARNING

September is historically the worst month for US markets. Do not be shocked if volatility increases.

The key risks to watch are US inflation data, West Asia tensions, and US bond yields. If the 30 year yield stays above 5.25 percent, FIIs will keep selling.

MORAL OF THE WEEK

The market fell for four straight weeks. Auto got crushed. IT saved the day. Small caps hit a record high.
Friday's bounce was real but do not FOMO into it.

When the market is confused, cash is your best friend. Keep some dry powder ready.
DIIs are buying everything FIIs sell. That is the only reason we are not at 22,000.

India's power infrastructure boom is creating another manufacturing cycle underneath it.

CG Power has rolled out the first transformer from its new greenfield facility at Sehore, Madhya Pradesh — a ₹792 crore investment designed to become India's largest single-location power transformer manufacturing facility.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗲

🏭 50-acre manufacturing campus

⚡ 45,000 MVA planned annual capacity

🔌 220 kV to 1,200 kV transformers

🏗️ Up to 35 power transformers per month

👥 2,000+ direct and indirect jobs expected

🌍 Domestic + export markets

The plant has begun operations with an initial installed capacity of 10,000 MVA, with the remaining capacity to be commissioned progressively.

At full scale, CG Power's combined transformer manufacturing capacity across its facilities is expected to reach 1,20,000 MVA annually.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗜𝘁 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀

Look at what's driving demand.

Renewable energy.

Transmission expansion.

Data centres.

Railways.

Industrial infrastructure.

Exports.

Every gigawatt of new generation and every major new power-consuming facility eventually creates demand for the infrastructure that moves and manages electricity.

𝗠𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗣𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿 → 𝗠𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗚𝗿𝗶𝗱𝘀 → 𝗠𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀 → 𝗠𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗘𝗹𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗘𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗽𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁

And CG Power's existing transformer plants are already operating at full capacity.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆

India's infrastructure investment cycle isn't creating opportunities only for power generators or EPC companies.

It's creating a parallel manufacturing opportunity for the companies supplying the equipment underneath those projects.

Transformers. Switchgear. Cables. Grid equipment. Storage systems.

As India builds more renewable capacity, transmission networks and AI data centres, electrical equipment could become one of the less visible — but critical — beneficiaries.

𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗮 𝗶𝘀𝗻'𝘁 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝗻𝗳𝗿𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲.

𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗹𝘀𝗼 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗹𝘆 𝗶𝘁.

Imho buying a growth co which steadily increases dividends might work better by year 5 or 10 because both might end up paying the same on cost basis. To each his own though. If done right, this style can get 9-10% returns, but the risk? Full year's dividend can be wiped out on 1 bad day

India is scrambling to rebuild coal stocks at power plants.

The government has asked captive mines and key Coal India subsidiaries to increase coal loading as inventories at some power plants tighten.

Coal India’s supplies rose 6.7% YoY to 322.9 million tonnes in the first five months of FY27.

But power demand has been growing even faster.

Electricity consumption has stayed above 10% growth since May, driven by cooling, irrigation and economic activity.

As a result, coal stocks at thermal power plants have fallen to around 28.6 million tonnes — from 59.3 million tonnes at the start of FY27.

Why does this matter?

India is producing more coal, but rising power demand is eating into the fuel buffer at power plants.

That makes reliable coal supply increasingly important for the thermal power sector, while higher loading and dispatch could support the coal mining and rail freight sectors.

The government is now coordinating coal, power and railway ministries to ensure the fuel actually reaches the plants.

The key thing to watch: whether stronger coal movement can rebuild power-plant inventories before demand rises further.

Common Sense Investing: The Damani-Blackstone Bet:  Horizon Industrial Parks

A Growth story Masked by Accounting Losses

Despite its flat debut and current stock price hovering slightly below the ₹60 IPO issue price, Horizon Industrial Parks presents a compelling long-term buying opportunity. The market's tepid response appears to be a short-term reaction that fails to recognize the company's strong underlying fundamentals and its transformation into a leaner, highly profitable entity poised for significant growth.

The Blackstone Foundation and Strategic Build-Up

Horizon Industrial Parks is not a typical startup; it is a meticulously built enterprise, engineered from the ground up by the global private equity giant, Blackstone. Over the last five years, Blackstone executed a strategic vision to create India's largest industrial and logistics infrastructure platform, expanding its potential nearly six-fold to a network of 45 "Grade A" facilities spanning 58.58 million square feet across 10 major cities. The recent IPO, which was a fresh issue of shares, was a crucial part of this master plan, designed to infuse capital and position the company for its next growth phase, internally dubbed "Horizon 2.0" .

Decoding the Losses: A Story of Growth Investment

The reported net loss of ₹203.65 crore in FY26 can seem alarming at first glance, but a deeper look reveals it is a structural artefact of a capital-intensive development model rather than operational failure. The company's core business is exceptionally profitable. In FY26, its operational EBITDA grew to an impressive ₹607.8 crore, achieving a stellar margin of 79.16% . The losses were solely due to heavy depreciation charges and a high interest burden from the debt used to fuel its rapid, five-fold expansion over the last five years.

The Tipping Point: Financial Deleveraging and a Profitable Future

The investment thesis hinges on the transformative use of the ₹4,250 crore raised through the pre-IPO placement (including from Radhakishan Damani) and the recent IPO. The company is using these funds to pay down approximately two-thirds of its debt. This strategic move is expected to cut its annual interest burden by over ₹300 crore. As finance costs plummet, management and analysts project that the company will achieve accounting net profitability starting Q4 FY27, with full-year profitability expected by FY28. This is the single most important catalyst for the stock.

Future Growth: A Clear and High-Value Roadmap

Horizon's operational strength is evidenced by an industry-leading committed occupancy rate of 93.56% across its 118 enterprise tenants. The quality of its tenant base is a key strength, with 54% of its leased space occupied by Fortune 500 companies, providing stable and predictable rental income. This high demand validates the strategic locations and Grade-A quality of its assets, making its future revenue stream highly dependable.

Future Growth: A Clear and High-Value Roadmap

The company's growth trajectory is built on a solid foundation of a fully paid-for land bank that allows it to double its operational footprint from ~30 million square feet to ~60 million square feet within the next 3.5 to 4 years. The future growth isn't just about scale, but also about a more lucrative product mix. Horizon is strategically expanding beyond traditional warehousing into higher-yielding Industrial Facilities (commanding a 10-15% rent premium) and In-City Centers (which can generate 2.5-3 times more revenue) . With a projected EBITDA aspiration of over ₹1,100 crore as operational capacity increases, the path to substantial earnings growth is clearly mapped out

Ace Investor Damani's Calculated Bet on Horizon

Radhakishan Damani's investment in Horizon Industrial Parks is a classic example of his signature strategy: identify a fundamentally sound business with a temporary, fixable problem, and enter well before the broader market catches on. His decision to invest ₹200 crore in the company's pre-IPO round reveals a well-considered, long-term bet on India's consumption and manufacturing growth story .

A Pre-IPO Entry, Not a Post-Listing 200 crore Bet

Damani did not buy his stake in Horizon after the IPO; he entered through a private placement in December 2025, eight months before the company went public . Together with other marquee investors like SBI Life Insurance and 360 ONE, he acquired shares at anaverage cost of ₹59.81 apiece, which was nearly identical to the IPO's final issue price of ₹60 . This means his current holding is essentially at par or slightly underwater, confirming this is a long-term position, not a short-term flip .

Investing in a Fixable Balance Sheet Problem

The reason Horizon is currently reporting losses is not due to poor operations—it's due to its massive debt load, which was used to fuel its rapid expansion. In FY26, the company's interest bill alone was ₹539 crore, which ate up nearly 78% of its revenue. Damani's thesis might be  that this is a fixable, structural issue. He is betting that by using the ₹2,600 crore IPO proceeds to pay down a significant portion of this debt, the company's interest burden will plummet. With an operational EBITDA margin of nearly 80%, the company is positioned to transition from a net loss to net profitability as early as FY28 . This is exactly the type of "value" situation Damani is known to favour: investing in a sound business obscured by a heavy debt burden.

Betting on a Blackstone-Built Platform and India's Macro Trend

Beyond the financial engineering, Damani is placing a bet on the strategic asset itself. Horizon, built from scratch by global private equity giant Blackstone, is India's largest industrial and logistics developer, with a 93%+ occupancy rate across its portfolio. Its future is not just about filling warehouses but also about diversifying into higher-yield industrial facilities (offering a 10-15% rent premium) and in-city centres (which can generate 2.5-3 times more revenue), driven by India's booming consumption and e-commerce markets.

A Bet That Aligns with His Investment Philosophy

Damani's investment style is rooted in his history as a bearish trader; his first question is always, "What can go wrong?" . In Horizon, the biggest risk—the debt—is a public and known quantity that is being directly addressed with the IPO proceeds. His plan isn't to make a quick profit but to hold for the long term, a strategy he has employed to build his immense wealth through companies like DMart . The near-zero immediate return on his pre-IPO investment is not a deterrent; it's simply the price of entry for what he perceives to be a high-quality asset in a high-growth sector

Coforge says one active deployment involves:

a U.S. clinical healthcare intelligence company

building:

**a sovereign AI environment.**

That concept matters for healthcare because workloads may contain highly sensitive:

clinical information
patient-related data
proprietary datasets.

Keeping the stack controlled by the organization can reduce reliance on external inference paths for certain workloads.

### 🏦 Banking deployment

Coforge also says a major U.S. bank is using managed model routing to:

reduce AI runtime costs

while retaining:

governance
auditability.

That reflects another frontier-AI problem:

different tasks do NOT need the same model.

Example:

simple extraction
↓
cheap/open model.

Complex reasoning
↓
frontier model.

Highly sensitive operation
↓
internal sovereign model.

The router becomes:

**the policy layer deciding where intelligence runs.**

### ⚙️ Six layers

Coforge packages the platform around:

Strategy & Advisory
↓
Infrastructure & Platform
↓
Model Engineering & Customization
↓
Deployment & Integration
↓
LLMOps + Observability + Guardrails
↓
Governance + FinOps + Managed Operations.

This matters because enterprise AI isn't only:

the model.

Production AI also requires:

identity
monitoring
cost control
deployment
evaluation
governance
security.

### 🧠 Why this matters

The first stage of generative AI was:

**rent intelligence through an API.**

The next stage may increasingly become:

rent some intelligence
+
own some intelligence
+
route between them dynamically.

That changes vendor lock-in.

Instead of:

application hard-coded to one model,

organizations may start building:

**model abstraction layers.**

### ⚠️ Important caveat

This is a:

Coforge commercial product announcement.

Claims around cost reduction, operational performance and governance effectiveness come from Coforge and its customer deployments and have not been comprehensively independently benchmarked.

Also:

“self-owned AI stack”

does NOT necessarily mean every model executing a workload is locally hosted.

The architecture can route to:

external frontier models

when policy permits.

The key idea is:

**control of the orchestration and policy environment**

—not necessarily complete elimination of third-party AI.

### 🛡️ Security implication

Model routing itself becomes a security control.

A sensitive request should not only ask:

“Which model gives the best answer?”

It should ask:

DATA CLASSIFICATION
↓
ALLOWED PROVIDERS
↓
ALLOWED REGION
↓
RETENTION POLICY
↓
MODEL TRUST LEVEL
↓
TOOL PERMISSIONS
↓
COST LIMIT
↓
route request.

That turns:

LLM routing

into:

**policy-based intelligence routing.**

### 🧠 CyberSignal insight

**The enterprise AI stack is beginning to look like cloud infrastructure did a decade ago.**

The winning architecture may not be:

one provider for everything.

It may be:

**a control plane that decides which intelligence runs which workload — under whose rules, on whose infrastructure and at what cost.**

Metal stocks under pressure: Nifty Metal falls 2.5% as Adani Enterprises, NALCO & Hindustan Zinc slide 📉

The Nifty Metal index fell around 2.5%, with several metal counters witnessing sharp selling in today's session.

Key movers:

• Hindustan Zinc: down up to ~10%
• NALCO: down up to ~8%
• Adani Enterprises: down ~6%
• Vedanta: under pressure
• Hindustan Copper: also declined

The sell-off comes amid a sharp rise in crude oil prices and broader risk-off sentiment across global markets. Higher energy costs are particularly important for the metals sector because smelting, refining and mining operations are energy-intensive.

But there is another important factor.

Several metal stocks had already delivered substantial gains, leaving valuations and positioning more vulnerable to profit-booking when global risk sentiment deteriorates.

From an RA perspective, the current correction needs to be viewed through three lenses:

1. Energy costs
Higher crude and power costs can squeeze operating margins.

2. Global metal prices
Copper, aluminium, zinc and steel prices remain key earnings drivers.

3. China & global demand
China's industrial activity and global infrastructure demand remain critical for base metals.

The sharpest moves are coming in stocks where expectations had already become elevated.

The key monitorables now:

• LME metal prices
• China demand data
• Crude & energy costs
• INR/USD
• Inventory levels
• Export/import trends
• Company-specific production volumes

A 2–10% decline in a single session does not necessarily change the long-term commodity cycle — but it does highlight how sensitive metal stocks are to changes in global risk appetite and input costs.

The next few sessions will reveal whether this is simply profit-booking or the beginning of a deeper sector-wide correction.

Q1 FY27: Company-by-Company Investor Notes

These 50 companies are at different stages of transformation. Some have started delivering earnings, while others are still building capacity, qualifying products or waiting for approvals. Each must therefore be judged separately.

Capital Goods and Engineering

1. Bharat Forge

Bharat Forge is transforming from a cyclical auto-forging company into a defence, naval, aerospace and advanced-engineering platform. Its large defence order book provides visibility, but overseas weakness and heavy capex remain concerns.

View: Strong long-term transformation, but accumulate only on corrections.

2. Happy Forgings

The company is shifting towards higher-value industrial, export and passenger-vehicle components. Its new heavy-forging press can address power, energy and data-centre demand, while margins remain above 30%.

View: Excellent execution, but current valuation offers limited comfort.

3. Ramkrishna Forgings

The railway-wheel venture, Mexico plant and casting acquisitions are beginning to contribute. Management is now focusing on utilization, cash flow and debt reduction after completing major capex.

View: Genuine turnaround, but debt must decline before conviction increases.

4. Sona BLW Precision Forgings

Sona BLW remains a leading EV-component company with a strong order book. Its DENSO partnership expands it into high-voltage motors and inverters, while robotics can become another growth engine.

View: High-quality long-term holding, but avoid chasing an expensive valuation.

5. TD Power Systems

Global shortages of generators and power equipment are driving strong export orders. AI data centres, grid stabilisation and renewable integration provide multi-year demand visibility.

View: Business momentum is exceptional, but valuation already discounts much of the supercycle.

6. Jyoti CNC Automation

Jyoti CNC is operating near full utilization and doubling capacity. Its large order book and import-substitution opportunity provide visibility across defence, railways and engineering.

View: Positive direction; monitor capacity ramp-up, working capital and cash flow.

7. Standard Engineering Technology

The core pharma and chemical-equipment business is growing, while data-centre infrastructure and specialised Japanese technology can create new revenue streams.

View: Exciting but early-stage. Wait for confirmed commercial orders.

8. Omnitech Engineering

Its order book is several times annual revenue, supported by multi-year global contracts. New facilities will expand machining capacity, but working-capital days remain very high.

View: Strong revenue opportunity, but cash-flow quality needs improvement.

Aerospace and Defence

9. Astra Microwave Products

A large radar-subsystem order has materially improved revenue visibility. The company participates in radar, missile, electronic-warfare and aircraft programmes.

View: Quality defence opportunity, but high receivables, long execution cycles and valuation are concerns.

10. AXISCADES Technologies

AXISCADES is selling legacy service businesses and redeploying capital into defence, aerospace and semiconductor equipment. The change can improve growth and margins.

View: Interesting special situation; wait for the divestment and capital-allocation plan to become clear.

11. MTAR Technologies

MTAR is growing across nuclear, clean energy, aerospace and data-centre infrastructure. Its order book is strong and working capital has improved.

View: Business inflection is real, but the extremely high valuation leaves no room for mistakes.

Auto and Auto Ancillaries

12. Ather Energy

Ather has entered positive EBITDA as electric-scooter demand accelerates. New products and capacity expansion can support a much larger scale.

View: Promising EV platform, but competition, cash requirements and execution risks remain high.

13. Sansera Engineering

Sansera is evolving from an auto-component company into an aerospace, defence and semiconductor supplier. Its advanced-systems order book provides strong visibility.

View: One of the better manufacturing transformations, but valuation demands near-perfect delivery.

14. Divgi TorqTransfer Systems

Divgi is expanding into automatic and manual transmissions, EV gearboxes, exports and local US manufacturing. Several large programmes will contribute from FY28 onwards.

View: Good long-term opportunity, but current earnings do not yet capture the required investments.

15. Steel Strips Wheels

The company is operating near full capacity, receiving price increases and adding alloy-wheel, knuckle and agricultural-wheel capacity. Exports are also recovering.

View: Strong operational momentum, but it remains cyclical and capital-intensive.

Metals and Industrial Infrastructure

16. Lloyds Metals & Energy

Lloyds Metals is transforming from an iron-ore miner into an integrated steel and metals company. New pellet, steel, copper and beneficiation capacities can expand earnings substantially.

View: Large opportunity, but equally large debt, capex and commodity risks.

17. DEE Development Engineers

Major capex is complete, and the company is entering the utilization phase. Its order book, turbine-piping relationships and seamless-pipe facility provide visibility.

View: Credible earnings inflection; monitor debt reduction and cash conversion.

18. Man Industries

The Saudi acquisition provides local manufacturing access and approved-vendor status in an important energy market. New facilities can expand products and margins.

View: Promising, but acquisition integration and working capital require confirmation.

19. Aeroflex Industries

Aeroflex is moving from flexible hoses into liquid-cooling assemblies for data centres. This new business already contributes meaningfully, and capacity is being expanded.

View: Genuine emerging data-centre opportunity; monitor confirmed orders and customer concentration.

20. Manaksia Coated Metals

The company is expanding colour-coated steel capacity while its existing line is almost fully utilized. Captive solar power should lower costs.

View: Measurable capacity-led growth, but steel prices and export demand remain risks.

Power and Electrical Equipment

21. CleanMax

CleanMax is building renewable capacity for large corporate and data-centre customers. Contracted projects and hyperscaler relationships provide demand visibility.

View: Strong structural opportunity, but project returns, funding costs and debt discipline are critical.

22. KSH International

KSH manufactures specialised transformer winding wires. Strong transformer demand and a long-term global supply agreement support capacity expansion and better margins.

View: Attractive indirect transmission-cycle play; track customer concentration and working capital.

23. Quality Power Electrical Equipments

The company is expanding into high-voltage equipment, winding wires, battery storage and insulators. Multiple new capacities and acquisitions can accelerate growth.

View: Strong opportunity, but execution has become complex. Wait for successful commissioning and integration.

24. Diamond Power Infrastructure

Diamond Power has recovered strongly from insolvency, with rapid revenue growth, a large order book and new cable capacities.

View: High-risk turnaround. Cash flow, equity dilution and working-capital needs matter more than revenue targets.

Chemicals and Advanced Materials

25. Aether Industries

Aether’s speciality-chemical and contract-manufacturing businesses are growing, while semiconductor materials and silicone technologies offer new platforms.

View: High-quality scientific business, but heavy capex, modest return ratios and valuation require patience.

26. Fineotex Chemical

The US acquisition has transformed Fineotex into a diversified speciality-chemical company with major oilfield exposure.

View: Strong potential, but ambitious targets depend on successful integration, margin improvement and cash generation.

27. Neogen Chemicals

Neogen is entering lithium salts and battery electrolytes. Early revenue, customer audits and capacity commissioning show progress towards commercialization.

View: Promising battery-materials platform; invest gradually because final approvals and funding needs remain significant.

28. Yasho Industries

Better product mix, customer commitments and improved utilization have expanded margins. New capacity can materially increase revenue over the next two years.

View: Credible inflection; watch whether higher margins remain sustainable as volumes rise.

29. Sudeep Pharma

The core pharmaceutical-excipient business is performing well. The larger opportunity is battery-grade iron phosphate for LFP batteries, but binding offtake agreements are still awaited.

View: Attractive optionality, but wait for commercial customer commitments.

30. Navin Fluorine International

Growth is broad-based across refrigerants, speciality chemicals and CDMO. Strong margins, net-debt-free status and multiple new growth projects provide financial comfort.

View: Among the highest-quality companies here. Accumulate gradually, preferably on corrections.

31. Himadri Speciality Chemical

Himadri is expanding into LFP cathodes, anodes, carbon nanotubes and speciality carbon black. Backward integration and internal funding are positives.

View: Powerful long-term transformation, but simultaneous projects create substantial execution risk.

32. Pondy Oxides & Chemicals

Pondy is expanding copper-cathode capacity while improving the value-added mix in lead recycling.

View: Attractive circular-economy and copper play, but metal spreads, scrap availability and working capital remain important.

Pharma and Healthcare

33. Aarti Pharmalabs

The company is expanding xanthine capacity while building a larger CDMO platform. Chinese supply restrictions support xanthine economics.

View: Good momentum, but sustainable CDMO growth is more valuable than temporary pricing benefits.

34. Senores Pharmaceuticals

Senores is expanding its regulated-market portfolio, US distribution and emerging-market registrations. Numerous product launches can support rapid growth.

View: Promising small pharma company, but regulatory execution and US price erosion require monitoring.

35. Granules India

Granules is shifting from high-volume products towards complex generics and peptide CDMO. Margins are improving and the balance sheet is nearly debt-free.

View: Attractive risk-reward, but regulatory clearance for its key facility remains the critical trigger.

36. OneSource Specialty Pharma

OneSource is becoming an important GLP-1 drug-device manufacturer. New cartridge lines can significantly expand capacity, with demand already strong.

View: Powerful opportunity, but promoter pledging, high receivables and limited normalised earnings history demand small position sizing.

37. Shilpa Medicare

After years of investment in biologics, peptides, formulations and CDMO, Shilpa is moving towards commercialization. Debt has declined and margins are improving.

View: Turnaround appears real, but product launches, cash flow and regulatory performance must confirm it.

38. Kwality Pharmaceuticals

Kwality is expanding into hormones, complex injectables and biosimilars. Several new plants and registrations can create additional revenue streams.

View: High-risk opportunity because guidance is aggressive and debtor days remain elevated.

39. Sakar Healthcare

Sakar is building an oncology-export business through dossiers, approvals and technology-transfer partnerships. Its existing facility provides capacity headroom.

View: Interesting early-stage opportunity; monitor approvals, exports and working capital.

Technology, Telecom and Data Centres

40. RateGain Travel Technologies

RateGain is becoming an integrated travel-technology platform covering customer acquisition, data, distribution and pricing. Margins and cash conversion are improving while acquisition debt declines.

View: One of the better growth-quality-valuation combinations. Suitable for staggered accumulation.

41. HFCL

HFCL has delivered a strong recovery through exports, optical-fibre demand and data-centre orders. Defence could become an additional growth engine.

View: Promising but speculative. Cash flow, debt and order conversion are more important than the headline order book.

42. Sterlite Technologies

Sterlite is repositioning as an AI data-centre connectivity company. A large hyperscaler contract has transformed its order book and revenue mix.

View: Important turnaround candidate, but customer concentration, receivables and execution need close monitoring.

43. Black Box

Black Box is directly participating in global hyperscale data-centre construction. Its large backlog and major customer wins provide multi-year visibility.

View: Preferred data-centre execution play at the right price. Monitor low margins, receivables and customer concentration.

Infrastructure and Logistics

44. Aegis Vopak Terminals

Aegis Vopak operates gas and liquid-storage terminals supported by long-term contracts. New pipelines and terminals can provide predictable growth.

View: Strong infrastructure franchise, but expansion is capital-intensive and valuation is demanding.

45. Shadowfax Technologies

Shadowfax is gaining logistics market share through express, same-day, dark-store and heavy-goods delivery. Growth is strong, but EBITDA margins remain below 5%.

View: High-growth platform, but not yet a proven high-margin compounder.

Financials

46. RBL Bank

A new strategic promoter and large capital infusion have strengthened the balance sheet. High-cost borrowings can decline, supporting margins and future growth.

View: Credible turnaround, but wait for better return on assets, margins and credit costs.

47. Muthoot Microfin

Collection efficiency, disbursements and asset quality are improving. Individual and gold loans can reduce dependence on traditional microfinance.

View: Attractive high-risk turnaround with a relatively comfortable valuation. Start small and add after confirmation.

Materials and Consumer Businesses

48. Borosil Renewables

Borosil is adding solar-glass capacity into a protected domestic market. Existing margins are strong, and the expansion can lift revenue materially.

View: Good near-term visibility, but profitability remains dependent on policy protection and solar-glass prices.

49. Shaily Engineering Plastics

Shaily has transformed into a healthcare-device company benefiting from GLP-1 and insulin injector demand. Healthcare is now its largest business.

View: Excellent structural opportunity, but much of the expected growth is already priced in.

50. United Foodbrands

The restaurant business is showing strong volume-led recovery, improving same-store sales and better store-level margins.

View: Promising consumer turnaround, but track whether growth, new-store economics and free cash flow remain sustainable.

🇮🇳 INDIA’S SEMICONDUCTOR STOCK UNIVERSE — WHAT’S ACTUALLY LISTED? 🧵

India’s semiconductor story is moving beyond just chip fabrication.

The ecosystem now spans chip design, OSAT/packaging, electronics manufacturing, engineering services and defence electronics.

Here’s a look at some listed names with semiconductor exposure 👇

1/10 — 🏭 OSAT / SEMICONDUCTOR PACKAGING

Companies directly involved in semiconductor assembly, testing or packaging include:

🔹 CG Power
🔹 Kaynes Technology
🔹 SPEL Semiconductor

This is one of the most important segments as India builds domestic semiconductor manufacturing capabilities.

2/10 — 💻 CHIP DESIGN & ENGINEERING

India has a strong advantage in semiconductor design and engineering talent.

Listed companies with exposure include:

🔹 MosChip Technologies
🔹 Tata Elxsi
🔹 HCLTech
🔹 Cyient

The opportunity here is less about manufacturing chips and more about design, verification, embedded systems and engineering services.

3/10 — ⚙️ ELECTRONICS MANUFACTURING

The semiconductor ecosystem doesn’t stop at the chip.

Companies such as:

🔹 Dixon Technologies
🔹 Syrma SGS

operate in electronics manufacturing and can potentially benefit as India’s electronics supply chain becomes more localised.

4/10 — 🛡️ DEFENCE ELECTRONICS

Semiconductors are critical for radar, communication systems, aerospace and defence electronics.

Bharat Electronics (BEL) is an important listed player within India’s broader strategic electronics ecosystem.

5/10 — 🇮🇳 WHY THIS THEME MATTERS

India has historically depended heavily on imports for semiconductors.

The policy push is now aimed at developing a domestic value chain covering:

Chip design → Materials → Fabrication → Packaging → Testing → Electronics

That is a much bigger opportunity than simply building fabs.

6/10 — 💰 GOVERNMENT PUSH

The semiconductor programme has evolved into a broader ecosystem strategy.

The focus includes:

🏭 Manufacturing
🔬 R&D
💻 Design
📦 Packaging
🧪 Materials
👨‍💻 Talent

The objective is to create a more resilient domestic semiconductor supply chain.

7/10 — 🌍 GLOBAL SUPPLY CHAINS ARE CHANGING

The semiconductor industry is increasingly becoming a strategic sector.

Geopolitics, supply-chain diversification and the push to reduce dependence on concentrated manufacturing hubs are creating opportunities for countries such as India.

India wants a larger role in this global value chain.

8/10 — 📊 THE BIG DIFFERENCE

Not every “semiconductor stock” has the same exposure.

Think of the ecosystem in layers:

Direct: OSAT / packaging / semiconductor manufacturing

Design: Chip design & engineering

Indirect: Electronics manufacturing

Strategic: Defence & advanced electronics

Understanding this difference is critical.

9/10 — 🔎 WHAT TO TRACK

For this entire theme, watch:

📌 Semiconductor project execution
📌 Capacity additions
📌 Government incentives
📌 Customer tie-ups
📌 Local sourcing
📌 Import substitution
📌 Global semiconductor cycle
📌 Margins & capital expenditure

The theme is long-term — execution will matter more than headlines.

10/10 — 🇮🇳 THE BIG PICTURE

India’s semiconductor opportunity isn’t just about “making chips.”

It’s about building an entire ecosystem around them.

Design + Materials + Manufacturing + Packaging + Testing + Electronics

That makes the semiconductor story one of the more important industrial and technology themes to track in India’s next phase of manufacturing growth.
